Chapter 10: Finding Peace—Living with Questions.
You know, for a lot of us, peace isn’t really about having a life without struggles. It’s more about learning how to live with the questions, to be okay with not having all the answers.
Think about the journey we’ve been on. It started with doubt, maybe even conflict. But instead of ending with absolute certainty, it leads us somewhere softer—a kind of acceptance. It’s that quiet confidence that tells you, “Hey, meaning can be found, even when things aren’t totally clear.”
Picture this: an adult child caught in the middle—caring for young kids on one side, and aging parents on the other. He stands right at the heart of his family’s story. And he’s stopped feeling like he has to pick a side between faith and skepticism. Instead, he honors both. He weaves together the rituals he grew up with, and the big questions he’s discovered as an adult.
The prayers, the old stories, the simple act of sharing a meal—these moments become more than just habits. They’re a way to mark time. They help us stay connected to the people we love, even as our lives keep changing.
Most of us don’t realize just how much peace there is in letting go of that craving for answers. The rituals, the acts of remembrance—they’re not just about tradition. They help us live with the uncertainty, and they bring real comfort when things feel unsettled.
In the quiet moments—maybe you’re lighting a candle, sharing food, or just holding someone’s hand—you start to see it. This whole journey isn’t about reaching some final destination. It’s about making peace with the questions themselves. It’s about finding meaning in the search, and honoring both where we’ve come from and where we’re headed.
So, as the story draws to a close, there isn’t a neat resolution. Instead, there’s hope. Even when we’re facing doubt and struggle, we can still find connection, a sense of belonging, and yes—even peace.
